title: Units: whole minor units per currency code, the currency table and its fallback, 26 or 27 pays a year spread so the year adds up, interest rounded half up, monthly amounts per pay
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 0, 3 (interest), 8 (units), 11 (the move's questions); DECISIONS_ROUND2 B4, B8, H9, I2, J1, E2, L (units q1 to q9), M8 to M10, N3, N4, O6, O, P4, R2
notes: Every amount is made up. Inputs typed by a person are text ("19.99"); everything else is whole minor units: yen 1 is 1, peso 1.00 is 100.

Question `to_minor`: a typed amount in a currency, as whole minor units with the currency's decimals and whether the screen must ask about the code. Question `currency_for`: the code from what an old copy or a person gave, or ask. Question `interest`: one month's interest on a balance at a yearly rate in percent [I2]. Question `pays_in_year`: the real number of pays a schedule has in a calendar year [H9]. Question `per_pay`: a monthly amount over that many pays, shown as the low and high per-pay amounts, how many get the high one, and the year's total. Question `period_amount`: what one pay period gets for a budget line or Free to spend by its `per` [B8]. Question `by_day`: with no fixed pay, what a monthly amount comes to over a number of days [B4]. Question `by_day_dates`: the same over dated days, each day rounded down and the remainder on the month's last day [L units q7]. Question `per_pay_list`: the amount of each pay of the year in order [L units q4]. Question `period_count`: the pay count a period uses [L units q3]. Question `load_amount`: a saved amount as it is loaded [L units q9]. Question `period_per_pay`: the amount of the pay that starts a period (`due`, its unshifted due date): its year, that year's pay count, its number in the year and its amount [N3]; a period that starts on 31 Dec with its pay due 1 Jan gets the next year's first amount. Question `week_by_day`: with no fixed pay, what a day gets from a `per: week` amount, and what the week's last day gets [M9]. Question `week_by_day_dates`: the same over dated days from `from` to `to`, for a line that started on `lineFrom`; a week ends on the seventh day counted from `lineFrom` [N4].

The currency table is the ISO 4217 minor-unit table, shipped with the page; an unknown code is 2 decimals and the screen asks once [L units q1]. A typed amount with more decimals than its currency is rounded half up, and `rounded: true` tells the screen to say so [L units q2].

Question `pays_in_year` also takes `{ rules: [ { from, rule } ] }`: each due date counted by the rule in force on it [O]. Question `home_cur_on` [O6]: the home currency on a date from the dated `home.curs`. Question `move_currency` [O, H9]: the move's currency answer from the raw stored 38.31 `ui` (`cur`, `preset`); ₱ with preset `legacy` or no preset, no currency at all, "$" and "¥" are asked.

Question `per_pay_rules` [P4]: a monthly amount for a schedule whose rule changes during the year (`rule.rules`). Each rule gets the months it is in force in that year (the first from 1 Jan): the monthly amount x those months, spread over that rule's pays, the leftover minor units on its earliest pays; `yearTotal` is 12 months. Question `period_per_pay` with `rule.rules` gives the pay's rule (`from`), that rule's pays, the pay's number among them and its amount.

[R2] A rule that changes on a day other than the 1st: the month of the change goes to the rule in force on its first day, and the new rule's months start the next month. Its pays still follow the new rule: every due date from the new rule's `from` is one of its pays, a pay in the month of the change included, and its months are spread over those pays.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: Yen has no decimals: 1 yen is 1
cases.why: Section 0: yen 1 is 1. The table gives JPY 0 decimals.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: Pesos have two decimals: 1.00 is 100
cases.why: Section 0: peso 1.00 is 100. PHP has 2 decimals, so 1 x 100 + 00 = 100.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: 19.99 pesos is 1999, read from the text
cases.why: 19 x 100 + 99 = 1,999. Worked as a decimal number, 19.99 x 100 is 1998.9999999999998, so a reader that cuts off instead of rounding would store 1,998. The digits are read as text.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: 0.29 pesos is 29

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: One decimal typed in a two-decimal currency
cases.why: USD has 2 decimals (the table in lookahead_ref.js): 1,234 x 100 + 50 = 123,450. ".5" is fifty cents.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: An unknown code: 2 decimals, and the screen asks once
cases.why: Section 0: an unknown code is 2 decimals and the screen asks once. 12 x 100 + 34 = 1,234, with ask set.

cases.question: currency_for
cases.title: A code is used as it is
cases.why: Every account, schedule, goal and budget line carries an ISO code (section 0); a code needs no question.

cases.question: currency_for
cases.title: "$" is asked, never guessed
cases.why: Section 0 and 11: "$" (dollars of many countries, and pesos are written with it too) is asked, never guessed.

cases.question: currency_for
cases.title: "¥" is asked, never guessed
cases.why: "¥" is yen or yuan; section 0 says it is asked.

cases.question: currency_for
cases.title: An old copy with no currency is asked, never set to pesos
cases.why: H9: old copies with no currency are asked, never set to pesos (the old default). The question comes before any amount is turned into minor units (section 11), because the decimals depend on it.

cases.question: interest
cases.title: 100,000 yen at 15% a year: 1,250 for the month

cases.question: interest
cases.title: 93,000 yen at 15%: half a yen rounds up
cases.why: 93,000 x 15 / 1,200 = 1,162.5. Half up to the minor unit gives 1,163 [I2]. (The same figure as interest.json's carried 93,000.)

cases.question: interest
cases.title: 123.45 pesos at 18%: under half a centavo rounds down
cases.why: 12,345 centavos x 18 / 1,200 = 185.175 centavos. The part after the minor unit is .175, under half, so 185 (1.85 pesos).

cases.question: interest
cases.title: A rate with a decimal: 14.6%

cases.question: interest
cases.title: Exactly half a minor unit goes up
cases.why: 100 x 6 / 1,200 = 0.5. Half up gives 1. Worked in whole numbers, so no decimal number can land just under 0.5.

cases.question: interest
cases.title: Under half a minor unit is nothing
cases.why: 1 x 6 / 1,200 = 0.005, under half of one minor unit, so 0.

cases.question: interest
cases.title: A credit carries no interest
cases.why: A balance at or below zero is a credit; J confirms no interest on a credit.

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: Every two weeks from Fri 1 Jan 2027: 27 pays in 2027
cases.why: 1 Jan + 14 x 26 days = 1 Jan + 364 days = Fri 31 Dec 2027, still in 2027. So 1 + 26 = 27 pays [H9].

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: Every two weeks from Fri 8 Jan 2027: 26 pays
cases.why: 8 Jan + 14 x 25 = 8 Jan + 350 days = Fri 24 Dec 2027; the next, 7 Jan 2028, is in the next year. 1 + 25 = 26.

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: A schedule that started in 2026 keeps its rhythm in 2027
cases.why: From Fri 13 Nov 2026: 27 Nov, 11 Dec, 25 Dec 2026, then Fri 8 Jan 2027 is the first in 2027. As units-19: 26 pays in 2027.

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: Weekly on Fridays: 53 pays in 2027
cases.why: 2027 starts on a Friday and has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day, so it has 53 Fridays: 1 Jan to 31 Dec. Section 8 says the real number of pays in that year; lookahead_ref.js uses 52 as its plain form, which is why this rule has its own file.

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: Twice a month: 24 pays
cases.why: Two days in every month (31 is the last day in shorter months, 10.8): 12 x 2 = 24.

cases.question: per_pay
cases.title: 30,000 yen a month over 26 pays: the year adds up to 360,000
cases.why: 30,000 x 12 / 26 = 13,846.15. Every pay gets 13,846 or 13,847. 13,846 x 26 = 359,996, so 360,000 - 359,996 = 4 pays get the one extra yen and the year adds up exactly to 360,000 [H9]. (Which 4: the earliest pays of the year, units-38 [L units q4].)

cases.question: per_pay
cases.title: The same 30,000 a month in a 27-pay year
cases.why: 360,000 / 27 = 13,333.33. 13,333 x 27 = 359,991; 360,000 - 359,991 = 9 pays get 13,334. Each pay is smaller than in a 26-pay year, but the year is the same 360,000. Using 26 in a 27-pay year would plan 13,846 x 27 = 373,842, about 4% too much.

cases.question: per_pay
cases.title: 300.01 pesos a month, paid twice a month
cases.why: 30,001 centavos x 12 = 360,012 over 24 pays = 15,000.5. 15,000 x 24 = 360,000, so 12 pays get 15,001 and the year is 360,012 centavos (3,600.12 pesos), 12 times the month.

cases.question: per_pay
cases.title: When it divides exactly, every pay is the same

cases.question: period_amount
cases.title: `per: pay` gets its amount each pay
cases.why: Section 8: a period gets the amount when `per` matches its kind. Every period is a pay period, so a per-pay line gets 20,000.

cases.question: period_amount
cases.title: `per: month` with monthly pay gets its amount, however long the period
cases.why: Monthly pay, monthly line: `per` matches, so 60,000 whether the period is 28 or 33 days (schema_review_1: never spread by days for a monthly earner).

cases.question: period_amount
cases.title: `per: week` over a 31-day period
cases.why: Section 8: `week` gets amount x days / 7 = 7,000 x 31 / 7 = 31,000.

cases.question: period_amount
cases.title: `per: week` with weekly pay
cases.why: A 7-day period: 5,000 x 7 / 7 = 5,000, the same as `per` matching.

cases.question: by_day
cases.title: No fixed pay: a monthly amount comes off by day
cases.why: Section 8 and B4: the monthly amount x 12 / 365 a day = 36,500 x 12 / 365 = 1,200 a day; 30 days = 36,000.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: Tunisian dinars have three decimals
cases.why: The full ISO 4217 table ships with the page [L units q1]: TND has 3 decimals, so 1 x 1,000 + 234 = 1,234, and the screen need not ask.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: Icelandic kronur have none
cases.why: ISK has 0 decimals in ISO 4217 [L units q1]: 1,500 is 1,500.

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: A code the short list did not have: Malaysian ringgit
cases.why: MYR is in the ISO table with 2 decimals [L units q1]: 12 x 100 + 34 = 1,234. It is known, so nothing is asked (before L it was treated as unknown and asked).

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: A typed yen amount with a decimal is rounded half up, and the screen says so
cases.why: Yen has no decimals. 1,234.5 is rounded half up to 1,235 and `rounded` tells the screen to say so [L units q2].

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: 12.345 pesos: half a centavo goes up
cases.why: PHP has 2 decimals; 12.345 is 1,234.5 centavos, rounded half up to 1,235 [L units q2].

cases.question: to_minor
cases.title: 12.344 pesos: under half a centavo goes down, still said
cases.why: 12.344 is 1,234.4 centavos; under half, so 1,234. It was still rounded, so the screen says so [L units q2].

cases.question: per_pay_list
cases.title: 30,000 a month over 26 pays: the extra yen go to the first 4 pays
cases.why: 360,000 / 26 = 13,846 with 4 left over (13,846 x 26 = 359,996). The leftover minor units go to the earliest pays of the year [L units q4]: pays 1 to 4 get 13,847, the other 22 get 13,846. 4 x 13,847 + 22 x 13,846 = 55,388 + 304,612 = 360,000.

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: A pay due Sat 1 Jan 2028, moved to Fri 31 Dec 2027, counts in 2028
cases.why: From Sat 2 Jan 2027 every 14 days: 2 Jan + 14 x 25 = 18 Dec, the 26th pay in 2027. The next is due Sat 1 Jan 2028; moved earlier it lands Fri 31 Dec 2027, but the count uses the unshifted due date's year [L units q3], so 2027 has 26.

cases.question: period_count
cases.title: A period that crosses 31 Dec uses its start year
cases.why: The period runs Fri 31 Dec 2027 to Thu 13 Jan 2028. It uses its start year [L units q3]: 2027, which has 27 pays on this rhythm (1 Jan + 14 x 26 = 31 Dec). 2028 would have 26.

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: The first year of a schedule set up in November counts the whole year by its rhythm
cases.why: Set up with its first pay on Fri 13 Nov 2026, it has only 4 pays in 2026 (13 and 27 Nov, 11 and 25 Dec). The first year counts by the rhythm [L units q5]: back from 13 Nov in steps of 14 days, the first on or after 1 Jan is Fri 9 Jan, and 9 Jan + 14 x 25 = 25 Dec, so 26.

cases.question: period_amount
cases.title: `per: week` over 30 days is rounded down
cases.why: 5,000 x 30 / 7 = 21,428.57, rounded down per period to 21,428 [L units q6]. Weekly amounts are a rate; nothing is carried to the next period and a year need not add up.

cases.question: by_day_dates
cases.title: No fixed pay, April 2027: each day rounded down, the remainder on 30 Apr
cases.why: 2027 has 365 days. A day is 30,000 x 12 / 365 = 986.30, rounded down to 986 [L units q7]. April's share is 30,000 x 12 x 30 / 365 = 29,589.04, 29,589 in whole yen; 29 days x 986 = 28,594, so 30 Apr gets the remainder: 29,589 - 28,594 = 995. 28,594 + 995 = 29,589.

cases.question: by_day_dates
cases.title: The same in a leap year: 366 days

cases.question: by_day_dates
cases.title: A stretch across a month end: April's last day carries its remainder, May has not ended
cases.why: 21 to 30 Apr is 10 days: 9 x 986 + 995 (30 Apr, with April's remainder) = 9,869. 1 to 5 May is 5 days at 986 = 4,930; May's last day is not in the stretch [L units q7]. 9,869 + 4,930 = 14,799.

cases.question: period_amount
cases.title: No fixed pay: `per: pay` is each money-in event
cases.why: With no fixed pay, `per: pay` means each money-in event [L units q7]: every time money comes in, the line gets 20,000.

cases.question: per_pay
cases.title: Weekly pay in a 53-pay year: the engine's real count, not the model's 52
cases.why: 2027 has 53 Fridays (units-21). 360,000 / 53 = 6,792 with 24 left over (6,792 x 53 = 359,976), so 24 pays get 6,793 and the year is 360,000. lookahead_ref.js keeps its plain 52 a year; the engine uses this file [L units q8].

cases.question: load_amount
cases.title: A saved amount that is not whole is kept as it is and flagged
cases.why: An old or hand-edited copy holds 1,234.5 where a whole number of minor units belongs. It is kept as it is (nothing is rounded on load, section 0) and flagged [L units q9].

cases.question: load_amount
cases.title: A whole amount loads with no flag
cases.why: 1,200 is a whole number of minor units: kept, no flag [L units q9].

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: A period that starts Fri 31 Dec 2027, pay due Sat 1 Jan 2028: the amount of that pay, 2028's first (was 2027's under M8)
cases.why: Every two weeks from Sat 2 Jan 2027: 2 Jan + 14 x 25 = 18 Dec 2027 is the last 2027 date; the next is Sat 1 Jan 2028, moved earlier to Fri 31 Dec, which starts the period. A period gets the amount of the pay that starts it [N3, which replaces M8's start year here]. That pay counts by its unshifted due date's year [L units q3], 2028, where it is the 1st; 2028 has 27 pays (1 Jan + 14 x 26 = 30 Dec 2028). 26,000 x 12 = 312,000; 312,000 / 27 = 11,555 with 15 left over (11,555 x 27 = 311,985), so pays 1 to 15 get 11,556 [L units q4]: 11,556. Under M8 it was 2027's 312,000 / 26 = 12,000.

cases.question: week_by_day
cases.title: No fixed pay, `per: week` of 5,000: 714 a day, the remainder on the week's last day
cases.why: A seventh of the week's amount each day, rounded down [M9]: 5,000 / 7 = 714.28, so 714. Six days of 714 = 4,284; the week's last day gets the remainder: 5,000 - 4,284 = 716. 4,284 + 716 = 5,000.

cases.question: week_by_day
cases.title: No fixed pay, `per: week` of 7,000: the same every day
cases.why: 7,000 / 7 = 1,000 exactly [M9]: nothing is left over, so the week's last day gets 1,000 like the others. 7 x 1,000 = 7,000.

cases.question: by_day_dates
cases.title: No fixed pay, January to March 2027: each month rounded down on its own, nothing carried
cases.why: A day is 360,000 / 365 = 986.30, so 986. January: 360,000 x 31 / 365 = 30,575.34, so 30,575; 30 x 986 = 29,580, and 31 Jan gets 995. February: 360,000 x 28 / 365 = 27,616.44, so 27,616; 27 x 986 = 26,622, and 28 Feb gets 994. March is as January: 995 on 31 Mar. Total 30,575 + 27,616 + 30,575 = 88,766. Nothing carries to the next month [M10]: the fractions (0.34 + 0.44 + 0.34) are lost, so the three months are not 360,000 x 90 / 365 = 88,767.12, 88,767.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: A period gets the amount of the pay that starts it: the 3rd pay of a year that has two amounts
cases.why: Every two weeks from Sat 2 Jan 2027: 2 Jan, 16 Jan, 30 Jan, so the pay due Sat 30 Jan is the 3rd of 2027. 2027 has 26 pays (2 Jan + 14 x 25 = 18 Dec). 30,000 x 12 = 360,000; 360,000 / 26 = 13,846 with 4 left over (13,846 x 26 = 359,996), and the 4 go to pays 1 to 4 [L units q4]. The period gets the amount of the pay that starts it [N3]: pay 3, 13,847.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: The 5th pay of the same year: the lower amount
cases.why: 2 Jan, 16 Jan, 30 Jan, 13 Feb, 27 Feb: the pay due Sat 27 Feb is the 5th of 2027. Pays 1 to 4 get 13,847 and the other 22 get 13,846 (units-54) [L units q4]. The period gets its pay's amount [N3]: 13,846.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: A period that starts Fri 31 Dec 2027 with a pay due Sat 1 Jan 2028: that pay's amount, 2028's first
cases.why: 2027 has 26 pays (last 18 Dec), so its two amounts are 13,847 and 13,846 (units-54). The pay that starts this period is due Sat 1 Jan 2028 and moved earlier to Fri 31 Dec; its count is by the unshifted due date's year [L units q3], 2028, where it is the 1st pay. 2028 has 27 (1 Jan + 14 x 26 = 30 Dec 2028). 360,000 / 27 = 13,333 with 9 left over (13,333 x 27 = 359,991), so pays 1 to 9 get 13,334 [L units q4]. The period gets the amount of the pay that starts it [N3]: 13,334, neither of 2027's two amounts.

cases.question: week_by_day_dates
cases.title: No fixed pay, `per: week` of 5,000 on a line started Wed 4 Nov: each week ends on a Tuesday
cases.why: A week ends on the seventh day counted from when the line started [N4]: Wed 4 Nov is day 1, so day 7 is Tue 10 Nov, and the next week ends Tue 17 Nov. Each day gets 5,000 / 7 = 714 rounded down; the week's last day gets the remainder, 5,000 - 6 x 714 = 716 [M9]. 14 days: 12 x 714 + 2 x 716 = 8,568 + 1,432 = 10,000, two whole weeks.

cases.question: week_by_day_dates
cases.title: The same line from Sat 7 Nov to Thu 12 Nov: Saturday and Sunday are ordinary days
cases.why: The line started Wed 4 Nov, so its weeks end on Tue 10 Nov and Tue 17 Nov [N4], not on a Saturday or a Sunday: Sat 7 and Sun 8 get 714 like any day. Sat 7 to Thu 12 is 6 days: Sat 7, Sun 8, Mon 9 get 714, Tue 10 gets 716, Wed 11 and Thu 12 get 714 [M9]. 5 x 714 + 716 = 3,570 + 716 = 4,286.

cases.question: pays_in_year
cases.title: Pay every two weeks to June, then monthly: each due date counts by the rule in force on it
cases.why: Every two weeks from Fri 1 Jan: 1 Jan + 14 x 12 = 18 Jun is the last before 1 Jul, so 13 pays; then the 25th of July to December, 6 pays. 13 + 6 = 19, each due date counted by the rule in force on it [O]. One rule for the whole year would say 26 (or 12).

cases.question: home_cur_on
cases.title: Before the change the home currency is yen
cases.why: `home.curs` holds yen from 4 Jan and pesos from 1 Mar [O6]; on 28 Feb the yen entry is in force.

cases.question: home_cur_on
cases.title: On the day of the change the home currency is pesos
cases.why: An entry holds from its own date [O6], so 1 Mar is pesos.

cases.question: home_cur_on
cases.title: Months after the change the home currency is still pesos
cases.why: The latest entry dated on or before 31 Dec is pesos [O6]; the yen history stays in yen.

cases.question: move_currency
cases.title: A copy holding ₱ with preset `legacy` is asked
cases.why: 38.28's clean-up writes ₱ and preset `legacy` into any copy with no currency (src/ui0.js normalize), so ₱ there may be a yen copy. The move asks [O].

cases.question: move_currency
cases.title: A copy with no currency recorded is asked
cases.why: The raw stored text (`frozen3831`) has no `ui.cur`, so no currency was ever chosen; the move asks, never pesos [O, H9].

cases.question: move_currency
cases.title: ₱ chosen with the peso sample is pesos
cases.why: The copy holds ₱ and was set up from the peso sample, so the choice is recorded: pesos, nothing asked [O].

cases.question: move_currency
cases.title: ¥ is still asked
cases.why: "¥" is yen or yuan, so it is asked, never guessed [H9].

cases.question: per_pay_rules
cases.title: Pay every two weeks to June, then monthly: each rule gets its own months, and the year adds up to 12 months
cases.why: The two-weekly rule is in force January to June, 6 months: 6 x 50,000 = 300,000, spread over its 13 pays (units-59): 300,000 / 13 = 23,076 with 12 left over (23,076 x 13 = 299,988), so 12 pays get 23,077 and one gets 23,076. The monthly rule is in force July to December, 6 months: 300,000 over its 6 pays, 50,000 each. 300,000 + 300,000 = 600,000 = 12 x 50,000 [P4]. A single count for the year (19 pays sharing 600,000) would give a monthly period about 31,579, not 50,000.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: The last two-weekly pay before the change gets its share of the first rule's months
cases.why: Fri 18 Jun is 1 Jan + 14 x 12, the 13th pay of the two-weekly rule in 2027. That rule has 300,000 for its 13 pays (units-67); the 12 leftover yen go to its earliest pays [L units q4, P4], so the 13th gets 23,076.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: The first monthly pay after the change gets the whole month
cases.why: Sun 25 Jul is the first pay of the monthly rule, in force from 1 Jul: 6 months, 300,000 over 6 pays, 300,000 / 6 = 50,000 for each [P4].

cases.question: per_pay_rules
cases.title: Two-weekly pay to Thu 15 Jul, then monthly on the 10th: July goes to the two-weekly rule
cases.why: The rule changes on Thu 15 Jul, not the 1st. On 1 Jul the two-weekly rule is in force, so July is its month [R2]: January to July, 7 months, 7 x 50,000 = 350,000 over its 14 pays (1 Jan, then every 14 days to Fri 2 Jul), 25,000 each. The monthly rule's months start in August: 5 months, 250,000 over its pays from 15 Jul, 10 Aug to 10 Dec, 5 pays, 50,000 each. 350,000 + 250,000 = 600,000 = 12 x 50,000.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: The last two-weekly pay before a mid-month change gets its share of seven months
cases.why: Fri 2 Jul is 1 Jan + 13 x 14, the 14th and last two-weekly pay before Thu 15 Jul. Its rule has 7 months (July included, R2), 350,000 over 14 pays, 25,000 each.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: The first monthly pay after a mid-month change, in the next month
cases.why: Tue 10 Aug is the monthly rule's first pay (10 Jul is before its start). Its months are August to December, 250,000 over 5 pays, 50,000 each [R2].

cases.question: per_pay_rules
cases.title: Monthly on the 25th from Thu 15 Jul: the 25 Jul pay is the new rule's, and its five months are spread over six pays
cases.why: July is the two-weekly rule's month, as in units-70 [R2]. The new rule's pays still follow it: 25 Jul to 25 Dec, 6 pays, and its months are August to December, 250,000. 250,000 / 6 = 41,666 with 4 left over (41,666 x 6 = 249,996), so the 4 earliest pays get 41,667 [L units q4]. The year: 350,000 + 250,000 = 600,000.

cases.question: period_per_pay
cases.title: The new rule's pay in the month of the change gets its first share
cases.why: Sun 25 Jul follows the new rule, so it is that rule's first pay of 6; its 250,000 gives the 4 earliest pays 41,667 [R2, L units q4].

cases.question: period_amount_once
cases.title: A one-period override is keyed by the pay that starts the period
cases.why: `once` names the period by its pay, pay@2027-01-10 [T1]: that period gets 55,000 instead of 40,000.

cases.question: period_amount_once
cases.title: Another period keeps the usual amount
cases.why: No override names pay@2027-02-10: 40,000 [T1, B8].

cases.question: period_amount_once
cases.title: A period started without its pay, on another day, still gets its override
cases.why: The pay due Sun 10 Jan was late and the person started the period on Tue 12 Jan (ps:pay@2027-01-10). The period is still pay@2027-01-10, so the override set before the pay landed still applies: 55,000 [T1]. Keyed by its start day it would have been lost.

cases.question: once_from_month
cases.title: A 38.31 one-month amount goes to the first period starting in that month (X watch: the stale 11.1 row)
cases.why: 38.31 `once['2027-03']`: the first period starting in March 2027 starts with the pay landing Thu 25 Mar, so `once` is keyed `pay@2027-03-25` [T1, X watch].

cases.question: once_from_month
cases.title: Weekly pay: four or five periods start in one month; the first one gets the month's amount (X watch)
cases.why: Periods start on Fri 5, 12, 19 and 26 Mar; the first is the one starting 5 Mar [X watch: `once[ym]` goes to the first period starting in that month].

cases.question: once_from_month
cases.title: Pay twice a month: the period starting on the 15th is the first in the month (X watch)
cases.why: The pay due 28 Feb landed Fri 26 Feb, in February; the first period starting in March starts Mon 15 Mar.

cases.title: A 38.31 one-month amount when no period starts in that month goes to the period holding that month's first day (Z5)
cases.question: once_from_month
cases.why: Pay is due on the 1st and moved earlier: the pay due Mon 1 Mar 2027 landed Fri 26 Feb and the next lands Thu 1 Apr, so no period starts in March. The period holding Mon 1 Mar started with the latest pay landing on or before it, the one due 1 Mar (landed 26 Feb): `once` is keyed pay@2027-03-01 [Z5].
